killed.claim: '--ease-standard… is an accelerate-then-decelerate curve designed for one-shot A→B transitions. Applied between the two stops of a symmetric loop it produces an asymmetric tick (slow-out on the way down, snap on the way back), not a breath.' (challenge-D-design.md:422-426)
killed.refutation: REFUTED twice over. (1) CSS Animations Level 1: animation-timing-function applies to EACH keyframe interval independently, not to the animation as a whole. offline-dot-pulse has stops at 0%, 50%, 100% (ApiOfflineChip.vue:82-85), so the identical curve governs the 0→50 leg and the 50→100 leg — the loop is symmetric by construction and no asymmetric tick can arise. (2) The curve is symmetric in kind: --ease-standard → --motion-ease-standard: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) (dist/styles/tokens/scheme-spring.css) is Material 'standard', an ease-IN-OUT, not an ease-in. The chosen token is the right shape for a breath.

killed.claim: 'chip fill (86,57,50) card well bg (86,57,50) → CR fill/well = 1.00… In dark mode the pill's background is pixel-identical to the card behind it. The 12%-destructive wash composites to nothing. There is no chip.' (challenge-D-design.md:90-100, 351)
killed.refutation: ARITHMETICALLY IMPOSSIBLE given the CSS, for any ground. ApiOfflineChip.vue:71 composites color-mix(in oklab, var(--destructive) 12%, transparent) — a 12%-alpha ink — over ground G, giving 0.12·ink + 0.88·G, which equals G if and only if ink == G. Dark --destructive = hsl(0 80% 60%) = (235,71,71) (dist/styles/tokens/dark-arm.css) and D's own sampled ground is (86,57,50): the composite must be ≈(104,59,53), an 18-unit red lift, not identity. D's own dark ink sample (brightest pixel 235,71,71) confirms the token resolved, which makes the coincident fill/well samples self-contradictory. Most likely cause is the caveat D itself recorded at :54-56 — the classList.add('dark') hack did not re-derive the ground. The dark limb does not survive; the light limb does (see confirmed).

killed.claim: '3.58:1 is the honest read of the perceived stroke body' for the offline chip's text; D-15 lists 'the lowest text contrast (3.58:1 offline)'. (challenge-D-design.md:104-117, 489-493)
killed.refutation: The offline register PASSES AA. ApiOfflineChip.vue:52 color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground) 72%, transparent) over the chip's own fill computes to (88,85,82) on (243,239,234) — and D's own 'darkest pixel (88,85,82) → 6.47:1' is an exact match for that computation, i.e. D measured the correct value and then discarded it. The 3.58 figure is the mean of the darkest 2.5% of ANTIALIASED pixels; WCAG 1.4.3 is evaluated against the specified foreground and background colours, not subpixel coverage deciles. Using the antialiasing decile manufactures a sub-AA number for a register that is 6.47:1. The real cause of the washout is a different defect — see my missed finding on synthesized small caps.

missed.claim: font-variant: small-caps is BROWSER-SYNTHESIZED in every code path — the shipped Fira Code webfont has no small-caps table. This, not ink opacity, is the actual mechanism behind the 'partial coverage on almost every glyph pixel' the design seat observed and mis-attributed to contrast.
missed.proof: ApiOfflineChip.vue:44 font-variant: small-caps (and DockStatusLamp.vue:52) resolve through .fira-code (demo/styles/utils.css:9-11) → --font-mono: var(--font-stack-mono) → '"Fira Code", "Fira Code Fallback", "Fira Mono", monospace'. The actual face glass-ui ships is node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/fonts/fira-code/fira-code-latin.woff2; read with fontTools its GSUB feature list is exactly ['calt','dnom','frac','locl','numr'] — no smcp, no c2sc. Browsers therefore synthesize small caps by scaling capitals, thinning stems to sub-pixel weight at 11px with 0.06em tracking. The component picked the one spelling the shipped font cannot honour. Present in both twins, so it is also a glass-ui BH/BI relay item.

Whether .dashed-well's rendered dark-mode ground matches its token computation. My refutation of D-8's dark limb rests on the compositing identity (0.12·ink + 0.88·G = G iff ink = G), which holds for any G and needs no live read; the specific dark RGB values I derived are not independently observed.

No r2 file exists for any axis in this component directory (only challenge-C/D/L r1 plus evidence/), so AXIS-PROMOTIONS does not apply here; all three are EXISTS-ORIGINAL per registry/HYDRATION-LEDGER.md:42-44, i.e. self-authored seats, not the thin Codex batch.
superlatives: The reduced-motion idiom is the best thing in the file and better than the app's own default. ApiOfflineChip.vue:81-90 puts BOTH the @keyframes body and the animation declaration inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), so under reduce no animation exists to override — strictly stronger than the blunt global guard at demo/styles/animations.css:184-192 (animation-duration: 0.01ms !important on *), which still runs a 0.01ms animation and still fights the cascade. All three axes credited this (challenge-C-implementation.md:400-406, challenge-D-design.md:433-435, challenge-L-library.md:359-361) and all three are right.

The animated property is opacity and nothing else (ApiOfflineChip.vue:83-84) — compositor-only, no layout, no paint — and there is no rAF, timer, listener or observer anywhere in the SFC. No cleanup surface, therefore no unmount race and no leak class. In a repo whose own constellation audit recorded a ~40-site PRM-RAF epidemic, this leaf is clean by construction.

The misconfigured ≠ unavailable distinction at the latch is genuine engineering, not ceremony. availability.ts:20-35 states the CORS-vs-network indistinguishability problem honestly, :112-116 detects the precondition up front rather than mislabelling a symptom, :167-169 refuses to relabel the designed state, and :188-191 fails loud and synchronously. The component's only sin is giving that distinction two visible surfaces where it needed at most one.

The DI seam is exemplary and should survive every cure unchanged. ApiOfflineChip.vue:31,35 reads the latch through useApiClient() rather than importing the module singleton, exactly as useApiClient.ts:2-17 intends, with a correct fail-fast when no provider stands above (:54-61). L's negative proof calls it 'the one structural decision in the file that is right' (challenge-L-library.md:404-406) and that is the correct read.

Self-gating with no empty shell: unknown and available render nothing at all (ApiOfflineChip.vue:12,20) — no zero-height node, no skeleton, no placeholder reserving space in the well. The absence is the design.

The copy tells the truth, and the truth was engineered to be tellable. 'saved locally' is backed by usePaletteActions.ts:65-77, where onCurrentPaletteSaved runs createPalette UNCONDITIONALLY, with a comment recording that the prior `await ensureUser()` inverted the contract and silently destroyed palettes on an unreachable backend. A status string that would have been a lie six waves ago is now a fact. No axis checked this; it is the strongest thing in the component's cone.

One line consumes a token correctly and gets a free accessibility win for it: border: 1px solid var(--card-edge) (ApiOfflineChip.vue:51) inherits the app's @media (prefers-contrast: more) arm, which lifts --card-edge from 12% to 55% ink (demo/styles/foundation.css:270, :736). It is the counter-example that makes the file's three dead var(--destructive, oklch(…)) fallbacks and its hand-mixed 72% ink legible as defects rather than style.

Cross-axis: the corpus's own best work is L's attribution proof (challenge-L-library.md:76-79), which settled the owner's OM-5 question by geometry — pad: 4.8px 8.8px and pos: absolute uniquely identify DockStatusLamp.vue:56,44 against ApiOfflineChip.vue:49,42 — rather than by assertion. It is the one measurement in 1,601 lines of challenge prose I could not shake, and it is the load-bearing fact under the BLOCKER all three seats share.

The live text is demo/DESIGN.md:64-65: "Two mechanisms, both required wherever live numeric values render **at display scale**:" — D's block quote truncates the sentence at "render:" and drops the scope clause, then applies the law to an 11 px `text-micro` readout, the SMALLEST type rung in the app (glass-ui scale.css `--type-micro: 0.6875rem`). The law's own preamble (DESIGN.md:62-64) states the harm it forbids — "dragging any component slider from min to max changes NO containing card rect (±0px)" — and no card rect moves here: ConfiguratorRow's header is `flex items-baseline justify-between` over a full-width row (configurator-M5OaIlJd.js), so a width swing re-truncates the sibling label inside a fixed box; the Card (ConfigSliderPane.vue:99-102) is unaffected. The `ch`-reservation limb is additionally contra-indicated by the app's own history: readoutReservation.ts retired per-cell `ch` min-width reservation because it "rendered the worst case as BLANK width on every non-worst value — 39–51% of every cell was empty reservation" (quoted in this megatranche's codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md:112, row M-21, ruled TRUE). The surviving obligation is the UNSCOPED sentence at VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:78, which binds mechanism 1 only — so D-7 stands as a tabular-figures finding and falls as a card-lock finding.

killed.claim: "Owner edict 5 violation (root-level styling, never per-instance override): a per-instance custom-property override that defeats the variant the same line requests" — and, in the design-system table, "`--slider-track-bg` per-instance override that defeats `variant="spectrum"` | the variant itself | violation (edict 5)".
killed.refutation: REFUTED IN PRODUCER BYTES, AND BY THE CORPUS'S OWN L AXIS. `--slider-track-bg` is not an override — it is the producer's PUBLISHED consumer hook, declared with a fallback in the recipe it is said to defeat: glass-ui.css `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-track { height: calc(var(--slider-thumb-size,1rem)*1.5); background: var(--slider-track-bg, var(--secondary)) }` (and the base `.slider-track { background: var(--slider-track-bg, var(--muted-medium)) }`). Feeding it is the sanctioned door, exactly as challenge-L-library.md:448-451 concludes from the same bytes: "The `--slider-track-bg` feed on line 202 is *correct* by contrast: a custom-property handoff, not a selector reach. That is the pattern the other three should follow." Nor does it "defeat" the variant: the empty fill is the producer's own spectrum recipe — `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-range { -webkit-backdrop-filter:none; box-shadow:none; background:0 0 }` — and holds whatever the track feed is set to. The real defect, which D-5's other two points state correctly, is choosing `variant="spectrum"` (a chromatic-rail recipe that delegates the value signal to a consumer-supplied ramp) for a non-chromatic domain and then supplying no ramp.

killed.claim: "the promise is awaited and discarded, so a rejected clipboard write is an unhandled rejection with no user-visible result."
killed.refutation: FALSE — `writeClipboard` never rejects. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/useClipboard-D36OTaeT.js:3-16: `async function r(e) { if (typeof navigator > "u" || !navigator.clipboard?.writeText) return { ok: !1, reason: "no-api" }; try { return await navigator.clipboard.writeText(e), { ok: !0 } } catch (e) { return console.warn("[useClipboard] clipboard writeText rejected:", e), { ok: !1, reason: "clipboard-api" } } }`. Every failure path returns a resolved result object, so awaiting-and-discarding cannot produce an unhandled rejection; the sibling axis states this correctly at challenge-C-implementation.md:343-346. The conclusion D draws (no user-visible result) survives via the correct mechanism — a discarded `{ok:false}` — but the named failure mode does not exist.

killed.claim: "31 sub-24 px targets; this pane *is* the app's tap-target outlier … WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 asks for ≥ 24×24 CSS px and has no pointer-type exemption; ConfigSliderPane.vue:218-230 gates its cure behind `@media (pointer: coarse)` and extends `block-size` only — the 12 px width is never addressed on any device."
killed.refutation: WRONG TARGET, AND THE EXCEPTION THAT APPLIES IS UNADDRESSED. (a) For a reka `Slider` the pointer target is the root/track, not the thumb: glass-ui.css gives the spectrum track `height: calc(var(--slider-thumb-size,1rem)*1.5)` = 24 px, and the sibling axis's own census measured that element at 432×24 (challenge-D-design.md:273, `cls: "slider-track", rect: 432×24`) — which meets 24×24 in both dimensions. The 12 px figure is the visual thumb (`width: calc(var(--slider-thumb-size,1rem)*.75)`), which PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:72 (§5 law 7) expressly separates from the operable target: "Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities. Accessibility floors do not require bloated visible chrome." (b) Even judging the thumb alone, SC 2.5.8's **Spacing** exception applies and BPC-6 never tests it: ConfigSliderPane.vue:215-217 sets `min-block-size: clamp(2rem, 7cqi, 2.625rem)` (32–42 px) per row, one thumb per row, so 24 px-diameter circles centred on adjacent thumbs cannot intersect. "No pointer-type exemption" is true and irrelevant — it is not the exemption in play. The proposed root-level cure would also inflate the producer's slider recipe for every consumer to fix a non-failure.

killed.claim: "**Propagation.** `geometry`/`surface`/`color` are re-spread into plain snapshot objects inside the computed, while `membrane`, `satellites` and `interaction` pass through as the live `reactive` proxy. The one slider that works (`membrane.smoothK`) is on the proxy side. … Both halves need the producer's read; the demo half is the snapshot."
killed.refutation: NOT ESTABLISHED, AND SELF-CONTRADICTING. The proxy/snapshot split is real in the bytes (HeroBlob.vue:152-178 spreads `geometry`, `surface`, `color` but passes `membrane`, `satellites`, `interaction` through the top-level spread as proxy references), but it does not predict the reported data: BPC's own table (challenge-C-implementation.md:29-30) shows the other two proxy-side atoms it tests, `warpAmp` and `noiseAmp`, at 5 px and 8 px — i.e. null — so 2 of 3 observations on the "working" side of the split refute the split as the explanation, and BPC concedes as much in the same paragraph before naming it a root anyway. It is also contradicted across axes: challenge-D-design.md:176 measures a SNAPSHOT-side atom (`surface.coreGlow`) at 6367 px / 4.91% while parked. The propagation mechanism additionally runs the wrong way for a snapshot: mutating `surface.coreGlow` DOES invalidate the computed (the spread reads that atom's keys), so a fresh config object reaches the prop, whereas mutating `membrane.warpAmp` does NOT invalidate it. Root 1 (construction) is arithmetic and stands; root 2 is a hypothesis presented as a finding. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE.

missed.claim: The entire "Pointer" section — all four sliders — tunes an interaction channel that has no pointer host anywhere in the app. This is a FOURTH, unnoticed root of the corpus's central BLOCKER, and it is pure source, needing no measurement.
missed.proof: BlobPane.vue:100-107 ships `interaction.pointerAttraction`, `pointerStrength`, `stretch`, `clickImpulse`. The producer binds the pointer field to a ref that is null unless the consumer opts in — node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/blob.js, Blob setup: `let … d = L("hitLayerRef"), f = w(() => !!t.pressLabel?.trim()), p = w(() => f.value && !t.disabled && !t.paused), m = w(() => p.value ? d.value : null), v = ve(m, { hitRadius: () => h })` — where `ve` is `useBlobPointer`, whose ONLY listeners are `e.addEventListener("pointermove", …)` / `"pointerleave"` on that same ref. The `.goo-blob-hit` button that would be that ref renders under `f.value ? … : T("", !0)`, i.e. only when `pressLabel` is a non-empty string. demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:13-19 passes `:color`, `:config`, `:paused`, `class` — and NO `pressLabel`; HeroBlob.vue:2-5 states the consequence in its own words: "Omitting pressLabel keeps the producer on its decorative canvas path—no button, focus target, **pointer host**, Tooltip, or duplicate Copy ownership." Belt and braces: HeroBlob.vue:10 wraps the whole thing in `<div class="pointer-events-none" aria-hidden="true">`, and glass-ui.css sets `.goo-blob-wrapper{…pointer-events:none;…}` and `.goo-blob-canvas{…pointer-events:none;…}`. So `m` is permanently null, no pointer listener is ever attached, `pointerActive` is永 false, and `clickImpulse` — driven by the hit button's `onClick: U` — has no emitter. `grep -rn "<Blob\b" demo` returns exactly one hit (HeroBlob.vue:13), so there is no other instance. CONSEQUENCE: combined with the four literal-overridden geometry atoms (D-3a/BPC-1/L-1), **8 of 31 sliders are provably inert from source alone**, before any idle-park or propagation argument. superlatives: Cross-package constant safety is airtight at BOTH ends. demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphere.ts:381 does `reactive(structuredClone(BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS))` and demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:93 does `Object.assign(config, structuredClone(defaults))` — the shared glass-ui module constant is never aliased into app state and never mutated by a reset. Mutating an imported defaults object is one of the most common and most invisible bugs in this shape; neither site commits it, and the useAtmosphere comment (:379-380) states the reason ("structuredClone so the reactive copy owns deep atoms").

`reseedHeroStops` (demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:117-130) is a genuinely well-built seam: ONE function shared by the live-colour watch (:132) and the KeepAlive re-activation (:246-250), with the invariant stated at :113-116 — "both write the SAME palette shape into `heroStops` — the wake path can never diverge from the live path" — and a `try/catch` that leaves the LAST GOOD ramp on an unparseable colour rather than blanking or throwing. The published-surface discipline is real and mechanically enforced. vite.config.ts:37-50 GENERATES the self-alias set from `package.json#exports` using ANCHORED regexes, with a header that records the exact prior bug a string alias caused (`@mkbabb/value.js/math` prefix-rewritten into the `dist/value.js` FILE → "Not a directory" → the R-era boot break). Verified consequence: `grep -rn '@src/' demo/` (excluding the exempt `assets/docs` embeds) and `grep -rn 'from "[./]*\.\./src/' demo/` both return NOTHING. The demo can only consume the published surface, and the alias set cannot drift from it.

No leaks in the idle gate: demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:227-230 `onScopeDispose` clears BOTH `idleTimer` and `poseTimer`, and the scrub detector windows its own buffer every tick (`changeTimes = changeTimes.filter(t => now - t <= SCRUB_WINDOW_MS)`, :270) so it cannot grow. Two of the three classic Vue timer/array leaks are pre-empted without ceremony.

`readPath` (demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:57-64) is null-safe on EVERY segment, not just the first: `if (cur == null || typeof cur !== "object") return undefined`. It is the reason a missing provider degrades to `undefined` instead of throwing inside the walk — and its care makes the write twin's asymmetry (L-11) conspicuous rather than symmetric sloppiness.

The `NumericAtomPath` guard (demo/scenes/blob/BlobPane.vue:19-52) is worth keeping even though BPC-4 is right that it has a hole. It DOES reject a typo and a boolean atom at compile time, and its comment reasons correctly and specifically about a subtle thing — that a homomorphic mapped type PRESERVES `?`, so indexing the mapped result injects `undefined` into the union, at BOTH nesting levels. That analysis is accurate for the `satelliteColors?`/`lightnessFloor?` leak it was written for (types.d.ts:115, :129). One token (`NonNullable<…>`) fixes the hole; the intent and the variance reasoning are better than anything else in this subtree.

demo/styles/foundation.css:648-698 is genuinely excellent design work: a documented two-tier `@media (forced-colors: active)` policy (U-F57 / BR-5) that refuses the blanket system-color substitution which would destroy a color tool's content, names a color-DISPLAY roster that keeps its real colors, leaves chrome at UA `auto` so it stays operable, and restores a system `Highlight` outline for focus because box-shadow rings cannot survive WHCM. Both URL/boot entry points are genuinely defensive. useColorUrl.ts:31-46 wraps parse+convert in try/catch and warns; hydrate.ts:98-130 falls through URL -> storage -> default on any throw, with a shape-validated localStorage read at :64-76. killed.claim: The mechanism of the Retry blank: "the availability latch is already tripped, so assertApiAttemptAllowed throws before any fetch; browsing returns to false within microtasks while the error leave is still in flight; out-in then holds isLeaving and the pending child never mounts. The faster the failure, the more certain the blank." (challenge-C-implementation.md:139-149)
killed.refutation: The symptom is confirmed; this causal chain is not established, and two of its consequences are wrong. (1) Vue 3.5.35 is built to recover from exactly this sequence: node_modules/@vue/runtime-core/dist/runtime-core.cjs.js:1412-1419 sets `leavingHooks.afterLeave` to reset `state.isLeaving` and call `instance.update()`, `instance.update` still exists at :6190, and the DEV_ROOT_FRAGMENT+transition case is special-cased in `remove` at :6659. I chased two candidate mechanisms and killed both: (a) EmptyState.vue's leading comment DOES compile to a two-root fragment (I compiled it with the installed @vue/compiler-sfc: patchFlag `2112 = STABLE_FRAGMENT|DEV_ROOT_FRAGMENT`), but :6659 handles precisely that, and (b) a missing instance.update is not the case in 3.5.35. So a completed leave should re-render the error plate; why it does not is unproven. (2) The environment premise the mechanism rests on is contested inside the corpus: challenge-C-implementation.md:8-11/75-77 asserts localhost is latched by detectDevMisconfig so no request is issued, while challenge-D-design.md:537-549 measured VITE_API_URL SET on the same machine, and demo/platform/transport/availability.ts:112 confirms `if (i.viteApiUrlSet) return false;` — the latch cannot fire there. Where the latch does not fire the second Retry issues a real fetch and fails SLOWLY, which the stated mechanism predicts would NOT deadlock — yet the D axis reports the blanking anyway (challenge-D-design.md:72). Conclusion: the mechanism is not the latch's speed. Consequence for the cure list: moves 1 and 2 (one status-discriminated surface; drop mode="out-in") remain sound because they remove the deferred-mount state entirely; move 3 (make Retry a refresh, `isSort=true`) is also sound but for a reason the pass does not state — useBrowsePalettes.ts:63-69 shows isSort=true sets sortLoading and never touches `browsing`, so the keyed branch never flips at all.

killed.claim: "Neither origin that boots the client can reach the API: localhost is latched by detectDevMisconfig so no request is ever issued" — the premise the whole pass-3 apparatus is built on (challenge-C-implementation.md:8-11, 75-89).
killed.refutation: Environment-dependent and false wherever VITE_API_URL is set, which is the first line of the predicate: demo/platform/transport/availability.ts:112 `if (i.viteApiUrlSet) return false;` (the full triad is documented at :106-117 — unset VITE_API_URL AND loopback page AND cross-origin base). challenge-D-design.md:537-549 measured that exact configuration on this machine and recorded the console as an ordinary CORS-blocked fetch surfacing as ApiUnavailableError. The two governing axis documents therefore disagree about the reproduction environment. This does not touch pass 3's findings (all of which I re-derived statically or accepted as probe evidence), but any future seat re-running probe-C3/* must first read `import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL`, or it will misattribute which error species reaches the pane — and the pane's headline copy "The commons is unreachable." is CORRECT for ApiUnavailableError and wrong only for the DevMisconfig arm.

demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:6-11 documents a genuinely subtle Vue-compiler hazard at the exact site where it matters: the list comment is deliberately the div's FIRST CHILD because a leading comment node would make the component multi-root and PalettesPane's `$el` read for useSortable would resolve to the comment. I verified the hazard is real by compiling a sibling file with the installed toolchain — demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue's leading comment compiles to patchFlag 2112 (STABLE_FRAGMENT|DEV_ROOT_FRAGMENT), i.e. a two-root component in dev. Someone here understood the compiler, wrote the reason down, and put the fix in the one file that needed it.

The transport's availability layer (demo/platform/transport/availability.ts:85-137) is a model of a designed degraded state: a pure, total, unit-testable predicate (`detectDevMisconfig`, :112-116) separating CORS-suicide from backend-down — two conditions the fetch layer collapses into one — plus a typed error per species and a 400-character message that names the exact command to run. That the pane throws all of it away at useBrowsePalettes.ts:79 (finding C-1) is the sharper indictment for how good the layer beneath it is.

demo/styles/foundation.css:653-696 and :830-841 declare ONE named colour-surface roster and reuse it across `forced-colors: active` and `@media print`, with the policy's intent written above it. Because the roster is one list with an `[data-color-surface]` extension point, D5-01 — the flagship defect on this component — has a one-line cure that fixes both media arms simultaneously. Centralising a policy so that its violations are cheap to repair is the whole point, and this file does it.

Resolution was proved in the same harness: `atoms.medium = { kind: "not-a-medium" }` errors TS2322 against the full 10-member union, and `const probe: string = atoms.medium` errors with the union's exact shape. TypeScript distributes over the discriminant, so the collapsed write is accepted. The ternary has no narrowing role; it is dead code, and D pass-1's D-13 and L's L-9 cure (`atoms.medium = { kind };`) are sound. C-17's INFO rationale for preserving the construct must not be carried forward.

killed.claim: "`--glass-accent` = `rgba(0,0,0,0)` (**DEFINED**, and transparent)" … "a **defined-but-transparent** `--glass-accent` (measured `rgba(0,0,0,0)` at `:root` in this app)".

This app declares `--glass-accent` nowhere: `grep -rn "glass-accent" demo/` → 0 hits. The definedness is the PRODUCER's own: `dist/styles/tokens/property-regs.css:1` registers `@property --glass-accent { syntax: "<color>"; inherits: true; initial-value: transparent; }`, and a registered property with an initial-value can never trigger `var()` fallthrough. That makes the defect universal — every glass-ui consumer that does not explicitly set `--select-dot-color` or `--glass-accent` ships an invisible selected state — rather than "any consumer under a transparent-accent root". Packet #4 must cite `property-regs.css:1`; a producer sent to look at this app's `:root` will find nothing there.

So P2-2's cure changes the affordance more than stated, and the 24×24 tap-target repair rests entirely on the `::before` inline-size term, not on the variant swap. (P2-C's core re-attribution — that the 12px inline extent is spectrum-only and therefore demo-chosen — is confirmed.)

superlatives: `demo/scenes/atmosphere/aurora-harmony-stops.ts` (40 lines, whole file) — the best idea in this component and one I have not seen elsewhere in the tree: every candidate harmony row previews the palette IT would resolve from the LIVE atoms, never a canned swatch. Its referent later drifted (C-2) — but the design instinct, and the fact that the file names the law it can be judged against, is why the defect is findable at all.

`demo/color-session/color-chips/PreviewStrip.vue` — `aria-hidden="true"` on a decorative specimen (`:39`), a `data-stops` stamp deliberately shared between chip and oracle (`:44`, `sample.ts:88-91`), a NAMED taste knob with its rejected alternative recorded inline (`STRIP_SEGMENT_CAP`, `:9-17`), honest truncation by mask-fade so a clipped palette reads as "continues" rather than as a complete palette it is not (`:73-75`), and a fixed golden proportion (`inline-size: 2.618rem` = φ²×1em, `:60-62`). Sixty lines that do everything right; the C axis's negative proofs 5 and 6 confirm it live.

`aurora-atoms.ts:15-52` — the `DEFAULT_AURORA_ATOMS` provenance block. Every constant carries the owner ruling that produced it, the bracket it landed inside, and the rejected alternative (the T-26 bracket closed from both sides; the T-32 rider's `scattered` prior with its measured x/y spreads). It records a real design invariant — the defaults carry NO `seed`, so Reset restores the SHAPE without disturbing the picked colour — which the C axis then verified live (negative proof 8). Documentation that makes an audit cheaper rather than longer.

`useAtmosphere.ts:283-290`, "THE NO-FIELD HONEST TERMINAL" — a degradation path that was DESIGNED rather than defaulted: on WebGL loss the persisted gradient ground IS the honest terminal, "never a blank canvas presented as a field", with a deliberate single re-arm on context-restore. This is the law C-1 correctly observes was written for the canvas and never extended to the controls — but the law itself is excellent, and it is why C-1 is expressible as a defect at all.

`ConfigSliderPane.vue:104-105` and `:159-162` — the W6-6 reasoning that moved the action bar OUT of the scroll region as a `flex-none` footer specifically so it can never occlude a slider or its readout. Second-order occlusion thinking of exactly the kind the enum block above it needed and did not get (D-2).

The corpus's own epistemic hygiene, which is above the norm and should survive the fold: challenge-D-design.md:287-355 is a standing "Corrections to pass 1" section that retires its predecessor's cure and kills its predecessor's `1/√φ` citation (correctly — I verified `PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:15` is Picker-scoped and `VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:78` names it the sole exception); challenge-C-implementation.md:622-627 records a HYPOTHESIS OF ITS OWN THAT WAS REFUTED (the `aria-label`-suppresses-value guess) with the raw CDP node as evidence, on the explicit ground that "a seat that only reports its confirmed guesses is not measuring."
